root_cause.text: The `cgroup_storage_get_next_key()` function incorrectly attempts to detect the end of a list by checking if `list_next_entry()` returns NULL, which is impossible because `list_next_entry()` wraps around to the list head instead of returning NULL.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff in `kernel/bpf/local_storage.c` replaces the ineffective NULL check `if (!storage)` with `if (list_entry_is_head(storage, &map->list, list_map))` after calling `list_next_entry()`, and the commit message explains that "list_next_entry() never returns NULL -- when the current element is the last entry it wraps to the list head via container_of()."

bic_trace_step.reason: The function `cgroup_storage_get_next_key()` contains the vulnerable construct. Specifically, on lines 262-264, it calls `storage = list_next_entry(storage, list_map);` and then checks `if (!storage) goto enoent;`. Since `list_next_entry()` wraps around to the list head instead of returning NULL, this check is ineffective and the function fails to detect the end of the list, leading to out-of-bounds or invalid memory access when it attempts to read `storage->key` later.
